name: nuremberg-landmarks
description: Historic landmarks of Nuremberg with era-by-era status for web map and Unity AR overlay

properties.name: Kaiserburg (Imperial Castle)
properties.blurb: The sandstone fortress above the old town, seat of Holy Roman Emperors.

1648.description: Still the emperor's castle, high above a walled Free Imperial City.

1939.description: A national monument. Rock cellars under the castle hill sheltered art treasures.

1945.description: Badly damaged; roofs and interiors of several buildings destroyed.

now.description: Rebuilt and open as a museum. Climb the Sinwell Tower for the view.

facts: The Golden Bull of 1356 required each new German king to hold his first imperial diet in Nuremberg.
Nuremberg first appears in written records in 1050.
The imperial crown jewels were kept in the city from 1424 until 1796.

properties.name: Albrecht Dürer's House
properties.blurb: Home and workshop of Germany's most famous Renaissance artist.

1648.description: A half-timbered house on the slope below the castle.

1939.description: A museum since 1871, one of the most photographed houses in the city.

1945.description: Heavily damaged in October 1944; rebuilt by 1949.

now.description: Restored and open to visitors with furnished rooms and a graphics workshop.

facts: Dürer lived and worked here from 1509 until his death in 1528.
He is buried in the Johannisfriedhof, grave 649.

properties.name: Hauptmarkt & Schöner Brunnen
properties.blurb: The central market square and its 19-metre Gothic 'Beautiful Fountain'.

1648.description: The Gothic Schöner Brunnen already stood at its edge.

1939.description: Renamed 'Adolf-Hitler-Platz' in 1933 and used for Nazi rallies.

1945.description: Houses around the square reduced to rubble; the fountain survived inside a concrete casing.

now.description: Rebuilt; hosts the Christkindlesmarkt every Advent.

facts: The fountain is about 19 m tall and decorated with some 40 figures.
Turning the seamless ring in its iron fence is said to bring luck.

properties.name: Frauenkirche (Church of Our Lady)
properties.blurb: Gothic hall church on the Hauptmarkt, famous for its noon clock show.

1648.description: Built for Emperor Charles IV. The Männleinlaufen clock paraded electors past the emperor at noon.

1939.description: A landmark of the Hauptmarkt; the daily clock show drew visitors from all over Germany.

1945.description: Badly damaged by the air raids, with much of the roof and interior lost.

now.description: Rebuilt. Every day at noon the Männleinlaufen clock sets seven electors in motion.

facts: The church stands where the synagogue stood until the 1349 pogrom.

properties.name: St. Sebaldus Church
properties.blurb: The oldest of Nuremberg's great churches, home to the bronze Shrine of St. Sebald.

1648.description: A Lutheran parish church holding Peter Vischer's bronze shrine of St. Sebald, finished in 1519.

1939.description: One of the twin great churches of the old town.

1945.description: Roof and vaults collapsed in the January 1945 firestorm; only the shell and towers stood.

now.description: Rebuilt in the 1950s, with the Vischer shrine back on display.

facts: The shrine was made by Peter Vischer the Elder and his sons between about 1508 and 1519.

properties.name: St. Lorenz Church
properties.blurb: Twin-towered Gothic hall church with Veit Stoss's hanging 'Angelic Salutation'.

1648.description: Lutheran since 1525. Veit Stoss's carved 'Angelic Salutation' hung in the choir.

1939.description: The great church of the southern old town, twin spires visible along the main shopping street.

1945.description: Roof and vaulting destroyed and the church stood open to the sky.

now.description: Rebuilt in stages after the war; the Angelic Salutation again hangs in the choir.

facts: Adam Kraft's tabernacle (1493-96) is about 20 m high.

properties.name: Old Town Hall (Altes Rathaus)
properties.blurb: Gothic and Renaissance town hall with medieval dungeons in its cellars.

1648.description: Newly extended (1616-22) in Italian Renaissance style. Envoys met here in 1649-50.

1939.description: Still the city's historic hall, its Renaissance front facing Rathausplatz.

1945.description: Largely burnt out. The medieval dungeons survived.

now.description: Rebuilt after the war. The Lochgefängnisse dungeons can be visited on guided tours.

facts: The Renaissance wing was designed by Jakob Wolff the Younger.

properties.name: Weißer Turm (White Tower)
properties.blurb: A medieval gate tower at the western end of the main shopping streets.

1648.description: A gate tower on the western approach to the inner city.

1939.description: A gate tower on the edge of the old town with busy shopping streets leading toward it.

1945.description: Damaged in the air raids that flattened much of the quarter around it.

now.description: Restored; still the western gateway to the pedestrian shopping streets.

facts: It was a gate in the older inner ring of the city walls, with origins in the 13th century.

properties.name: Heilig-Geist-Spital
properties.blurb: A hospital built across the river Pegnitz, once guardian of the imperial crown jewels.

1648.description: A charitable hospital arching across the river. Its church held the empire's crown jewels from 1424.

1939.description: A familiar riverside sight in the old town.

1945.description: Burned out in the raids; only parts of the structure remained.

now.description: Rebuilt; its arches again span the Pegnitz.

facts: In 1796 the crown jewels were evacuated ahead of French troops; today they are in Vienna.

properties.name: Henkersteg & Weinstadel
properties.blurb: The covered 'Hangman's Bridge' beside the half-timbered Weinstadel.

1648.description: A covered wooden footbridge beside the old wine warehouse, named for the executioner's tower nearby.

1939.description: A postcard favourite: half-timbered houses, covered bridge and river.

now.description: Reconstructed in 1954 and again one of the city's classic views.

facts: The bridge is named for the hangman, whose quarters stood nearby.

properties.name: Königstor & Handwerkerhof
properties.blurb: The round gate tower at the railway-station entrance to the old town.

1648.description: A massive round gate tower in the wall, with moat and bastions around it.

1939.description: The gateway between the railway station and the old town.

1945.description: The gate tower was damaged but survived.

now.description: Restored. The Handwerkerhof, a craft-market village built in 1971, welcomes visitors.

facts: The Handwerkerhof is a modern creation from 1971, not an original medieval quarter.

properties.name: Hauptbahnhof (Central Station)
properties.blurb: Hub of Germany's first railway city, where the Ludwigsbahn began in 1835.

1648.description: Not built yet. Beyond the walls there were only moat, gardens and fields.

1939.description: A major rail hub; special trains brought huge crowds to the Nazi Party rallies.

1945.description: Railway targets were bombed repeatedly; the station and yards around it were badly damaged.

now.description: Rebuilt and modernised. The DB Museum next door tells the story of German railways.

facts: Germany's first public steam railway ran between Nuremberg and Fürth in 1835.

properties.name: Germanisches Nationalmuseum
properties.blurb: Germany's largest museum of cultural history, in a former Carthusian monastery.

1648.description: The Carthusian monastery, founded in 1380, still stood here after the monks left.

1939.description: Germany's largest cultural-history museum, built around the old monastery.

1945.description: Heavily damaged by bombs, though much of the collection had been moved for safekeeping.

now.description: Rebuilt and expanded. See Martin Behaim's 1492 'Erdapfel', the oldest surviving terrestrial globe.

facts: The Way of Human Rights (1993) is a row of 30 columns inscribed with the articles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

properties.name: Palace of Justice & Nuremberg Trials
properties.blurb: Courtroom 600, where the Nazi leaders were tried in 1945-46.

1648.description: Not built yet. Open land outside the city, well west of the walls.

1939.description: Built in the early 1900s as the city's main courthouse.

1945.description: Damaged but largely usable; chosen by the Allies for the International Military Tribunal.

now.description: Still a working court. The Memorium Nuremberg Trials museum opened in 2010.

facts: The main trial ran from 20 November 1945 to 1 October 1946, with 22 defendants judged.
Twelve were sentenced to death, seven to prison terms, and three were acquitted.

properties.name: Zeppelin Field & Tribune
properties.blurb: The Nazi Party's main parade ground, designed by Albert Speer.

1648.description: Not built yet. Forest, ponds and farmland southeast of the city.

1939.description: The stage for the Nazi Party rallies (1933-38): vast choreographed parades before a stone grandstand.

1945.description: On 22 April 1945 US Army engineers blew up the giant swastika on the tribune.

now.description: A protected monument. The city works on how best to preserve and explain the site.

facts: The tribune was inspired by the Pergamon Altar in Berlin.

properties.name: Congress Hall & Documentation Center
properties.blurb: The Nazis' unfinished colossal congress hall, now a history museum.

1648.description: Not built yet. Only the shore of the Dutzendteich pond lay here.

1939.description: Construction began in 1935 for some 50,000 seats but stalled with the outbreak of war.

1945.description: Never completed and left as a shell.

now.description: The northern wing houses the Documentation Center Nazi Party Rally Grounds (opened 2001).

facts: The hall was never roofed; its brick and granite shell stands as a monument.

properties.name: Johannisfriedhof (St. John's Cemetery)
properties.blurb: Medieval cemetery with the graves of Albrecht Dürer and other Nuremberg greats.

1648.description: Famous for flat sandstone graves with bronze epitaphs. Dürer had been buried here in 1528.

1939.description: A tree-shaded cemetery just outside the old town and a place of pilgrimage for Dürer admirers.

1945.description: Air raids caused some damage but the cemetery largely survived.

now.description: Still in use and open to visitors; look for Dürer's grave (no. 649).

facts: Veit Stoss is buried here too.
